question: Elephantiasis, also known as lymphatic filariasis, is caused by ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**parasitic worms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elephantiasis, or lymphatic filariasis, **is a painful and disfiguring condition. Infection with parasitic nematodes (roundworms) of the family Filariodidea is transmitted through **mosquito bites**.
 
• Mosquito-transmitted larvae land on the skin and can then enter the body. The larvae subsequently travel to lymphatic arteries, where they mature into adult worms, thus perpetuating the transmission cycle.
 
• The main symptom of elephantiasis is gross enlargement and swelling of an area of the body because of the accumulation of fluid. The arms and legs are the areas most often affected. An entire arm or leg may swell to several times its normal size resembling the thick, round appearance of an elephant's leg.
 
• **Parasitic worms, commonly known as helminths**, are huge macroparasites with adults visible to the human eye.
 
• Many of them are soil-transmitted intestinal worms that infect the gastrointestinal tract.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bacteria** are single-celled organisms with a small size. Bacteria can be found practically everywhere on the globe and are essential to its ecosystems.
 
• **Protozoa **are microscopic unicellular eukaryotes with a complex internal structure and a wide range of metabolic functions.
 
• **A virus **is a type of infectious microorganism that consists of a nucleic acid segment (DNA or RNA) encased in a protein coat.
